summary: Proceed, but F2's equivalence gate has to be rewritten before the build. As written it compares align2's tables torch.equal against SGLang's moe_align_block_size, and they never match on any routing with remote routes, so F2 would always gate OFF and verify_32 would read flat for a spec reason. The wgmma kernels are layout-agnostic, so align2's tables are correct for them. The fix is a semantic check (master's own per_expert logic) plus a bitwise check on the _moe_wgmma output.
justification: A. F2 mechanism is real. kernel_fn sends 256..512 tokens to _moe_wgmma whenever wg_on_256 is set (master's logs show B256 WGMMA in all four archived runs). _moe_wgmma still runs expert_map[topk_ids.to(int32)] and SGLang's moe_align_block_size(local_ids, 16, count). Meanwhile master's align2 v256 flag (chunk 64, 4.70 vs 6.46 us at bsm 32) only reaches _moe_marlin, which is dead code at bs=256. Replacing a ~11.8 us 4-launch front end with a ~4.7 us 2-launch one is about 7 us of ~405 us (~1.7%). That is below the row-level drift, so the profile rows are the evidence and the headline is not. EXTRA_NOTE check, which is the weakest link. SGLang's moe_align_block_size(local_ids, bsm, 32) gives remote (-1) routes padded m-blocks of their own, with block_experts = -1. Master's self-check logs this as r_pad > n_pad DIFF in most cases (e.g. T=8 all-remote n_pad=0 vs r_pad=64; triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack's review counted 48/60 cases DIFF). SGLang's within-expert order also comes from atomics. align2, like _align_small and _align_parallel, drops -1 routes, orders routes ascending within an expert, uses capacity n + count*(bsm-1) instead of SGLang's n + (count+1)*(bsm-1), and writes -1 past the used blocks. So n_padded, sorted_ids[:n_padded] and block_experts[:n_padded/16] are NOT torch.equal to master's wgmma front end on any routing with a remote route, and every judged routing has them (32 of 256 experts local). Is this a correctness bug in the outputs? No. I read the wgmma consumers. (1) wg_gather returns for slot >= n_padded and for be outside [0, n_experts), and zero-fills sentinel slots (sid >= num_routes). align2's sentinel is n = numel, the same value SGLang uses. (2) wg_kernel reads min(n_padded/16, blocks_len, MAXB) block_experts and treats any id outside [0, n_experts) as non-local. (3) Its chunks are maximal runs of one local expert cut every 8 blocks, so per-expert chunk sizes and the run-time wgmma N choice match SGLang's layout exactly; only block positions shift. (4) The w2 epilogue scatters to cache3[route], and the post-norm masks by local_ids, which is identical. (5) The host checks hold: at T=512, align2 has 286 blocks (<= WG_MAX_BLOCKS 384), and sorted_ids.numel() 4576 <= WG_CAP_ROWS 8192, with block_experts.numel()*16 >= sorted_ids.numel(). Swap-AB rows are independent dot products over the same K order, so the _moe_wgmma output should be bitwise equal. The table-equality step of the gate is the part that is wrong. Required amendment: drop torch.equal on n_padded, sorted_ids and block_experts. Replace it with master's _align_self_check per_expert semantics against SGLang: per-expert sorted route multisets equal; per-expert block counts equal over the be >= 0 blocks; n_padded == 16 * sum of local blocks; block_experts[:used] all >= 0 and non-decreasing, with -1 for the tail; sentinel fill (count of n == len - real, none > n); local_ids torch.equal; n_padded/16 <= WG_MAX_BLOCKS. Then keep full _moe_wgmma output torch.equal against master's _moe_wgmma, falling back to rel-L2 <= 1e-3 if torch.equal ever fails on an order-only cause; never gate on finiteness alone. Equivalently, compare align2 at bsm 16 torch.equal against _align_parallel at bsm 16, which master already validates per-expert against SGLang, and that suffices. F1 (w13 atomic at T=1): measured twice on the judge, +2.5-3%. However, its gate is rel-L2 vs master (8.4e-3), and master already carries its own error vs fp32. At T=1 the only row is the whole output, under a 1.5% bound. Require F1's self-check to also measure rel-L2 vs an fp32 reference (C1b already has a dequant reference to build on) and stay OFF above ~1.0e-2 vs fp32. C1a/C1b: each was measured at about +0.5-1% at decode_32, and the gate ratios are plausible (_align_parallel 2.6 vs _align_small 3.55-4.3 us; align2 d32 is OFF on master at ratio 1.000, so the incumbent is _align_small). Expected directions agree with TASK.md: all six loads have weight 60, and only bs=1/32/256 should move. The ~+0.85% headline is inside the ±1.5% CI. The conjecture's decode_32 'graph-gap' test is weak: one run cannot tell 'less than the sum of kernel deltas' from ±1-2% row drift. Only the profile rows (kernel us) can tell kernel savings from gap savings, and only roughly.
confounders: align-two-phase-port-from17: provides the _align_two_phase kernels F2 reuses. Its v256 gate and timing ran at bsm 32 against _align_parallel on the Marlin path, not at bsm 16 against the SGLang front end. Its 1.374 ratio does not transfer, so F2 needs its own bsm-16 warm, equivalence and timing (the hypothesis does plan this).

align-parallel-per-expert-verify / triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack: they established that the dropped-remote-blocks layout is the master norm on the Marlin path. Their logs (r_pad > n_pad) are why F2's torch.equal-vs-SGLang gate cannot pass. On the wgmma path, removing SGLang's -1 blocks also shortens the block_experts scan and the gather grid's work, so a small part of any verify_32 gain could come from that rather than launch count. It is visible as wg_gather / wg_kernel rows moving by more than 0, and is not a reason for a companion.

triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack (the _align_small at <=32 path): C1a replaces exactly this at 17..32. On that base most of the earlier align gains were Marlin work removed (fewer m-blocks), but _align_parallel and _align_small produce identical layouts. So C1a's gain is align kernel time only, and the Marlin row should be unchanged; if it moves, that is drift.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: sets SMALL_M_POST_NORM = 32, so T == 32 still uses SGLang's fused norm. C1b replaces exactly that one shape, so there is no overlap, but C1b and C1a land on the same shape (decode_32) and cannot be separated by the headline.

w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m: w2 at T=1 already runs atomic (state w2_mode). F1 adds atomic on w13 at T=1, so both Marlin calls at decode_1 now use atomic reduction, and F1's error stacks on w2's. This is why F1's gate must be vs fp32, not vs master alone.

cuda-nvfp4-wgmma-rega-grouped-s5-copy-safe-bucket-gate (BEST, master's wgmma path): F2 changes only its front end. If wg_on_256 comes out False in this run (the selector timed under prepare noise), F2 is moot and verify_32 runs Marlin with align2 v256 as on master. Read the B256 PATH CHOSEN line before attributing anything at bs=256.
interference: No companion is warranted. The three sources are shape-disjoint: F1 is T==1, C1a/C1b are 17..32 and T==32, and F2 is the wgmma bucket only. Each has its own prepare-time gate that prints PATH CHOSEN with medians, and bs=8/16/128 are byte-for-byte master controls. Attribution comes from the profile rows: at bs=256 the index_elementwise / unrolled_elementwise / moe_align_block_size / count_and_sort rows should be gone and _align2_count / _align2_place present; at bs=32, _align_parallel_kernel and _post_norm_combine_hoisted_kernel should appear; the bs=1 Marlin row should sit near 33.7 us. An ab-revert of any landed hypothesis would not make a gain or a loss easier to read. The only intra-shape ambiguity is C1a vs C1b at decode_32, and the kernel rows already separate it; a control would cost a scored run to settle a <1% split that is inside drift. The real risk to interpretability is F2 silently gating OFF because of the table torch.equal; the required gate amendment fixes that, not a companion.
rules_flags: No rules violation in the design. kernel_fn branches only on shape and prepare-set plain ints (wg_align2, d32_align, d32_post_norm, F1 flag). There is no per-call mutable or process-global state and no BLAS/cuBLASLt preference toggling.

_align_two_phase allocates a cnt scratch per call, sized from shape only (nchunks x num_e). That is allowed (shape-sized, not value-sized) and is the same as master's Marlin-path use. Ensure every (T, chunk, bsm=16) constexpr variant is warmed in prepare, so no Triton compile happens during capture: NCH_P2 changes with T.

F1 numerics: at T=1 the whole output is one row under a 1.5% bound. Gate it on rel-L2 vs an fp32 reference (not only vs master's bf16 path, which has its own error), with margin. Otherwise a routing worse than the self-check's could fail a judged call.

Prepare budget: the combo phase start deadlines (120/150/160/170 s) begin after master's _wg_setup, which may run to its 200-255 s deadlines. If master's prepare overruns ~120 s, every combo phase skips itself and the run measures master. Print per-phase elapsed time so a skip reads as a skip, not as 'no gain'.
open_questions: F2 gate (required change): replace the torch.equal on n_padded / sorted_ids[:n_padded] / block_experts[:n_padded/16] vs SGLang's moe_align_block_size with per-expert semantic equality (master's _align_self_check per_expert logic), or with torch.equal against _align_parallel at bsm 16. Then keep the bitwise _moe_wgmma output check against master's front end. Under the spec as written, every routing with a remote route fails and F2 is always OFF.

Does the bsm-16 align2 at T=256 actually beat SGLang's front end by about 2x in the component graph? It was measured at bsm 32 against _align_parallel, not against the 4-launch SGLang path. Also time _align_parallel at bsm 16 as a second candidate: it is already validated, and at v128 it beat align2 (ratio 0.781).
Does master's prepare finish early enough (< 120 s) for all four combo phases to start? The log's per-phase seconds will tell.
Is wg_on_256 True in this run? If the B256 selector flips to Marlin, F2 is moot and bs=256 measures master's Marlin+align2 path.
F1: what is the rel-L2 vs fp32 at T=1 on the skewed routing with both w13 and w2 atomic?
